A target or a cue is visible in all three ride modes — Power, HR-Zone and Route — on a data-only trainer.

A 40-minute ride on the 800IC produces a diagnostics export that still contains its connect-time block, including the 0x2ACC bits and the Indoor Bike Data flags word.

Field evidence is sought: an internal-testing build is offered to Paul Evans with a ride in each mode requested; his reply, or its absence after the offer, is recorded on ISS-0405. Not gated on his answer.

The rider manual in the sibling repo has pages for riding a bike the app cannot control and for the pacer ghost, in English and the eight locale copies, passing the translation-parity check.
A rider with no Google Play can install the app from the repository and receive an update through it.
A purchase issues a key that unlocks PRO offline, with no network call at any point.
The developer is not the merchant of record and files no VAT return for it.
The Play build is unchanged in behaviour and contains no alternative payment path.
Both signing keys are backed up somewhere that survives the loss of the development machine.

Restoring equipment after a ride does not cost one tap per device. *(Evidence: `reconnectAll()` on both; `ScanViewModelReconnectAllTest`.)*

Every acceptance check on a moved surface carries a dated invalidation event naming this work. *(Evidence: 52 Android and 71 iOS events naming CHG-20260922 in the working ledgers; five regression checks split (TST-0669..TST-0673).)*

phases.name: One ride history across a household's tablets

items.text: A ride recorded on one tablet is in the other tablet's history for the same rider, with the same duration, the same numbers and the same per-second trace, and neither tablet ever shows it twice.
A rider's personal bests read the same on both tablets, and they were recomputed on each rather than copied.
A ride a rider deletes stays deleted on the tablet they deleted it on, through any number of later reads.
Nothing Your Trainer did not record appears in any rider's Your Trainer history, however many other apps upload to the same account.

A rider's weight, FTP, LTHR, max HR and resting HR read the same on both tablets and on intervals.icu, and a rider who turned the send option on can change them in either place without losing the other side's value.
A rider who has no intervals.icu account can still do everything they can do today, and no surface offers them a sync they cannot have.
A ride uploaded by either platform still opens correctly on intervals.icu, on Strava and in Garmin Connect, with its laps as laps.
No request is made on behalf of a rider who has not connected an account.
`PARITY_MATRIX.md` shows every surface this phase touched, on both platforms, and none of its rows went into deficit.

Ramp intervals expressible in YTW format — `WorkoutInterval.targetPowerEndPercent` (`data/models/WorkoutProgram.kt:152`), sample `docs/samples/ramp-warmup.ytw`. ([[TASK-0235]], [[REQ-0059]])

Coaching text events display during workouts — `CoachingCue` (`data/models/WorkoutProgram.kt:175`) fired per interval in `WorkoutViewModel.kt:2083-2109`; `effectiveDurationSec` guards the Gson-bypassed default ([[ISS-0292]]). ([[TASK-0236]], [[REQ-0060]])
Repeat groups flatten correctly at runtime — `IntervalDeserializer.kt:30` expands `{repeat, intervals}` at parse time; sample `docs/samples/repeat-groups.ytw`. ([[TASK-0237]], [[REQ-0061]])
ZWO files importable and converted to YTW — `utils/ZwoParser.kt`, wired through `utils/WorkoutImporter.kt`. ([[TASK-0239]], [[REQ-0063]])

Published JSON schema validates all workouts — `docs/ytw-schema.json` ships and was realigned to the shipped format by [[CHG-20260529-YtwSchemaDocRealignment]]. Re-checked 2026-07-26: all 77 workouts in `assets/workouts/` carry every `required` key. **Known drift:** the corpus also carries `geoTrack` (FEAT-0080 route polyline), which the published schema does not yet describe — the schema under-describes the format rather than rejecting it. ([[TASK-0238]], [[REQ-0062]])

Cadence targets shown during structured workouts — target RPM + deviation colouring + directional prefix in `ui/ActiveWorkoutScreen.kt:1416-1438`, reading `WorkoutInterval.cadenceTarget`. ([[TASK-0061]], [[TASK-0064]], [[REQ-0054]])
Spiral of death relief automatically reduces power — `ui/viewmodels/WorkoutViewModel.kt:390` (state) and `:2280` (relief logic). ([[TASK-0063]], [[REQ-0055]])

Rider card renders with 6 attributes and overall rating — `ui/components/RiderCard.kt` (PWR / SPR / CLB / END / CON / **HRE** + 0–99 rating badge; the sixth axis is HR-efficiency, `RiderCard.kt:304`, weighted 10% in `utils/RatingEngine.kt:69`).
Attributes computed from actual ride history — `utils/RiderAttributeCalculator.kt` derives each axis from stored sessions.
Ratings scaled against pro cyclist benchmarks — `utils/RatingEngine.kt` benchmark anchors.
Card visible on profile and selection screens — rendered from `ui/UserSelectionScreen.kt` and `ui/WorkoutSelectionScreen.kt`.
Empty state for riders with <5 sessions — `RiderAttributeCalculator.MIN_SESSIONS = 5` (`:20`) returns null below the threshold (`:39`, `:59`), which drives the card's empty state.
NP/TSS/IF/VI visible in workout history session cards — four `TrainingMetricCard`s in the expanded session card (`ui/WorkoutHistoryScreen.kt:1774-1777`, TASK-0094).
Peak power values displayed in session detail — 5s / 30s / 1m / 5m / 20m peak bars (`ui/WorkoutHistoryScreen.kt:1782-1787`, TASK-0095).

Metrics hidden when values are null — the metrics block is gated on `if (np > 0 || tss > 0f)` (`:1760`) and the peak list is `.filter { it.second > 0 }` (`:1788`), so a session lacking power data renders neither.
TSS color-coded by training load — `tssColor` thresholds at 150 / 300 (green → amber → red) applied to the TSS card (`ui/WorkoutHistoryScreen.kt:1769-1776`).
Three tabs (Power / Route / Heart Rate) on Workout Selection.
Each tab has a Free Ride entry + structured workout library.
HR-Zone structured workouts run from the library (at least the 18-workout bundled set).
Routes can be imported from GPX, FIT Course, TCX files.
Route workouts run against the trainer with simulation resistance driven by interval grade.
All three editors gated Pro/Family; authoring works for Pro riders.
Room migration v19 → v20 ships cleanly with no regressions on existing Power workouts.
All existing Power acceptance tests continue to pass unchanged.
GPX import creates rideable course — `utils/RouteGpxImporter.kt` (with `RouteFitImporter` / `RouteTcxImporter` alongside), producing `WorkoutProgram.routeProfile`.
Trainer resistance changes with gradient — grade drives FTMS SIM via `WorkoutViewModel.onSimParamsChanged` (`:804`) and the control path at `:837-888`.
Multi-lap looping works — lap-relative state in `WorkoutViewModel.kt:369`; the cockpit's `inMultiLapVisual` switches the power line to lap-running/ride-long/max (`ui/ActiveWorkoutScreen.kt:1391`).

ERG fallback works on power-only trainer — `ergFallbackDesired = !supportsSimParams && slopeMode != RESISTANCE` (`WorkoutViewModel.kt:861`), fed from `ScanViewModel.supportsSimParams` (`MainActivity.kt:620-624`).
Ghost rider replays personal and family best laps — `GhostRepository.getFamilyBestLaps` (`WorkoutViewModel.kt:929-931`) plus the rider's own PB lap.

Ghost overlay visible on 2D elevation terrain during ride — `ui/RouteTerrainView.kt:107-115` positions each ghost at `ghost.distanceAt(lapElapsedSec)`; tier filtering happens in the caller (FREE → empty, PRO → own PB, FAMILY → all), per TASK-0108.
PB card appears on session-end overlay for repeated structured workouts — `PersonalBestCard` in the completion overlay (`ui/ActiveWorkoutScreen.kt:2298`).

Workout library and history show PB badges for the current rider — library cards take `personalBest` per `programId` (`ui/WorkoutSelectionScreen.kt:117`, `:1410`, rendered at `:2620`); history surfaces the PB through the thread card's `pbSessionId` rather than a per-row badge (below).

History groups repeated attempts of the same workout into a thread card with PB metric visible — `HistoryRow.Thread` (`ui/viewmodels/WorkoutHistoryViewModel.kt:204-214`) groups on `programId` once there are ≥2 attempts and marks the PB attempt via `pbSessionId`; free-ride threads carry no `pbSessionId` because the PB table is keyed on `(riderId, workoutProgramId)`. ([[FEAT-0063]])
iOS app published on App Store
Feature parity with Android for core workout functionality
All iOS hardening issues (ISS-0070–0099) resolved
Acceptance tests passing on iPad
Unlinked riders see the official "Connect with Strava" button (delivered via Strava's `btn_strava_connect.png` asset — replaces the generic Material Link button).
Linked riders see the "Compatible with Strava" brand mark next to a Material Switch (Strava-orange track when on) on Profile → Connected.

Uploaded history rows show a tappable pill — `View on Strava` when `stravaActivityId` is known (specific-ride deep-link), `Open in Strava` when not (athlete training feed fallback). Strava's attribution is for apps that *display* Strava data (segments, activity detail, leaderboards). Our integration is upload-only + outbound deep-links; we never render Strava data locally, so the attribution doesn't apply. The "Compatible with Strava" logo on the row already signals the integration. Revisit if we ever add a surface that renders Strava-sourced data.

Failed uploads surface a bounded error state — OkHttp connect / write / read timeouts (30/90/60 s) + explicit `SocketTimeoutException` handling + WorkManager retry (3×) + a `Retry` pill on the session row. (ISS-0112)

Session restored from backup reconciles its `stravaUploadStatus` against the Strava API via `StravaRepository.reconcileMissingActivityIds` — runs on rider-select + a manual `Refresh` button on the Profile's Strava subsection. (ISS-0142)
Rides deleted on Strava's side are detected on the next reconciliation sweep — the session's status flips back to unset so the `Upload` pill reappears and `Upload all` can re-send it. (ISS-0125)

Every user-visible English string in the app is sourced from `strings.xml` (no hardcoded literals in Compose code outside brand-name proper nouns) — guarded at unit-test time by `i18n/HardcodedComposeTextTest.kt`, whose regex set covers named-arg literals plus `body` / `subtitle` / `actionLabel` / `message` / `hint` / `errorText` / `prompt` / `confirmText` / `dismissText`.

Settings → Language picker lists the 9 Tier-1 locales and applies the change without an app restart — `i18n/LocaleManager.kt` (`setUserChoice` `:51`, `applyPersistedLocale` `:139`) + `ui/components/LanguagePickerDialog`. The activity *recreates*; the process does not restart. Acceptance: `docs/tests/ACCEPTANCE_TESTS.md` "Locale picker — switch end-to-end".

Device-locale auto-detect on first launch picks the matching Tier-1 locale; falls back to English when device locale isn't in the set — `AppLocale.resolveDeviceLocale` (`i18n/AppLocale.kt:55-57`), covered by `i18n/AppLocaleTest.kt`. The non-Tier-1 fallback path also raises a dismissable banner (TASK-0462).

AI-generator output for a non-English-locale user has its workout name, description, and interval cues emitted in the user's current locale (and the workout file's `primary_locale` matches) — covered by `data/remote/WorkoutAiServiceLocaleTest.kt`.

Imported foreign-locale workouts on an LLM-enabled device show the "Translate" banner; tap → strings cached into the workout's `strings.<locale>` block — `ui/components/RuntimeTranslateBanner.kt` wired at `ui/WorkoutEditorScreen.kt:2230`; retry/refresh behaviour covered by `data/translate/WorkoutTranslateRetryTest.kt` and `ui/viewmodels/WorkoutEditorTranslateRefreshTest.kt`.

On a no-LLM device (BYOK key absent or tier doesn't allow AI), the Translate banner / Settings toggle / bulk action are all hidden — the banner is a no-op unless the caller passes `isVisible` (`RuntimeTranslateBanner.kt:53`); gating coverage in `ui/viewmodels/TranslateBannerCoverageTest.kt`.

Settings → Language → "Spotted a translation issue?" feedback link present (TASK-0461). Replaces the prior "beta cohort validates a sample of strings per locale" exit criterion — riders self-report per-locale issues directly to support@your-applications.com via pre-filled email (locale + version + template body).

Tier-1 acceptance tests added for: locale-picker switch, workout-schema round-trip, AI generator locale tagging, translate-banner gating — all four exist: `docs/tests/ACCEPTANCE_TESTS.md` "Locale picker — switch end-to-end" (manual), `data/models/WorkoutSchemaRoundTripTest.kt`, `data/remote/WorkoutAiServiceLocaleTest.kt`, `ui/viewmodels/TranslateBannerCoverageTest.kt`.

A seat pin that resolves cannot be changed; one that does not resolve re-establishes per the arrival-state table, and `ON DELETE SET NULL` is proven by test. — `Migration34To35Test.deleting_the_seated_rider_frees_the_pin_rather_than_dangling` (emulator, green); iOS equivalent `LicenseSeatPersistenceTests.testDeletingTheSeatedRiderFreesThePin` (8 cases, green).

Upgrading via `pro_to_family` restores every hidden rider with no data loss, proven by test. — `LicenseSeatResolverTest.upgrading PRO to FAMILY restores everyone with no write` and the iOS twin. The **real SKU purchase** remains a manual acceptance row.
Room migration v34 → v35 has an exported schema and a passing `MigrationTestHelper` test. — `app/schemas/…/35.json` exported; `Migration34To35Test` 6 cases green on an API 35 emulator.

The grandfathering decision in RISK-0009 is recorded — either way, explicitly, not by default. — Edwin, 2026-09-10: existing PRO owners are **not** given multi-rider. They keep the full app for one rider, and a second rider means the `pro_to_family` upgrade. Recorded in [[RISK-0009-ProReadsAsDowngrade]] § 2.

REL-0017's gate section carries no number. [[TASK-0897-GenerateTheSheetAndRetireTheRunPlan]].)*

The survey section names Equipment Hub, the riding cockpit, Trainer compatibility, Developer Options and route selection, each with the PHASE-021 or FEAT-0117 tasks that changed it. *(The survey is grouped by surface note, so these appear as Hardware, Riding — structured, Riding — simulation and Riding — routes, with TASK-0826, 0864, 0833 to 0835, 0828, 0829, 0844, 0883 to 0885 and 0836 named.)*

ISS-0001.title: Dashboard: PERF dial spacing
ISS-0001.lead: The "PERF" and "ENERGY" metrics should be distributed into two equal columns, with each metric centered within its assigned half of the row.

ISS-0002.title: ERG Smoothing: Jump at threshold
ISS-0002.lead: The ERG Smoothing logic does not provide a seamless transition between intervals. It appears to "jump" to the target wattage once the next interval's threshold is reached, rather than completing a smooth linear ramp.

ISS-0003.title: Redundant Add Rider Button in Selection Screen
ISS-0003.lead: Rider Selection screen has an "Add Rider" button at the top, but also has "Add Rider" placeholders in the list. The top button is redundant and should be removed for a cleaner UI.

ISS-0004.title: Settings Appearance Mode Expansion
ISS-0004.lead: Settings currently only toggle Dark Mode. It should support three distinct modes: System Default, Light, and Dark.

ISS-0005.title: Strava Link Not Working
ISS-0005.lead: The Strava integration link does not function correctly.

ISS-0006.title: Starred Workout Styling
ISS-0006.lead: Starred (favorite) workouts currently have an "ugly big border," which distracts from the list view. A more subtle visual indication, such as shading or a colored background, is preferred to differentiate them.

ISS-0007.title: Bluetooth Disconnect After Workout
ISS-0007.lead: The Bluetooth connection to the trainer/sensors remains active after the workout has finished. To save battery and allow for clean reconnections, the devices should be disconnected upon workout completion or exit.

ISS-0008.title: Workout Screen Mode Color Sync
ISS-0008.lead: When switching between ERG and Resistance mode, not all colors update. Specifically, the terrain view and play/pause buttons should reflect the mode's accent color (e.g., TrainerGreen for Resistance).

ISS-0009.title: Workout Card Visual Refinement
ISS-0009.lead: Workout cards have a large border that can be removed for a cleaner look. The workout icon (mini-graph) can be slightly larger.

ISS-0010.title: Equipment Selection Icons
ISS-0010.lead: The Trainer and Heart Rate monitor selection slots lack descriptive icons.

ISS-0011.title: Persistent Workout Duration Mismatch
ISS-0011.lead: Despite previous attempts to fix JSON durations, some workouts still display 32 minutes instead of the correct 34 minutes (e.g., Threshold Over-Unders). This is likely due to stale data in the local database or the UI relying on a non-calculated totalDuration field.

ISS-0012.title: Transition Warning Color Mismatch
ISS-0012.lead: The timer color during the 10-second transition warning does not match the intensity zone color of the upcoming interval.

ISS-0013.title: Transition Beeps Timing Error
ISS-0013.lead: The countdown beeps during the interval transition do not play every second as expected.

ISS-0014.title: Transition Audio Improvements
ISS-0014.lead: There is no audio cue when the 10-second transition warning starts. The final transition beep (T-0) sounds like two small beeps and feels cut off.

ISS-0015.title: Paywall Screen Gaps: Missing Family Tier and Functional Buy Buttons
ISS-0015.lead: The current Paywall screen does not display the "Family" tier option, and the purchase buttons (labeled "Select") do not clearly indicate a purchase action. Additionally, "Restore Purchase" functionality is not wired up.

ISS-0016.title: OpenAI URL Duplication (Redundant 'chat' suffix)
ISS-0016.lead: Users reported that OpenAI API calls were failing with 404 errors or malformed URLs when custom base URLs were provided.

ISS-0017.title: AI Workout Generation Cast Exception
ISS-0017.lead: During acceptance testing, attempting to generate an AI workout results in a crash/error: java.lang.Class cannot be cast to java.lang.reflect.ParameterizedType.

ISS-0018.title: Entitlement State Propagation Issues
ISS-0018.lead: After a successful purchase of Pro or Family tiers, the application state does not correctly update to reflect the new capabilities in the UI, even if the underlying logic allows some features.

ISS-0019.title: Lost Workout Selection during Trainer Pairing
ISS-0019.lead: When a user selects a workout without a trainer connected, the app prompts to connect a trainer but loses the workout selection in the process.

ISS-0020.title: Improper Device Filtering in Workout Selection Flow
ISS-0020.lead: When a user selects a workout without an active trainer connection, the application brings up a pairing dialog that displays both Trainers and Heart Rate Monitors, allowing for accidental incorrect selection.

ISS-0021.title: Missing Upgrade Path from Pro to Family License
ISS-0021.lead: Users who have already purchased an individual "Pro" license do not have a clear or functional path to upgrade to a "Family" license.

ISS-0022.title: Favorites Functionality Inoperable
ISS-0022.lead: The ability to mark a workout as a "Favorite" is not working as expected during acceptance testing.

ISS-0023.title: Inefficient Device Connection Flow on Workout Selection
ISS-0023.lead: When a user selects a workout without an active trainer connection, the app currently opens a device selection dialog. This is suboptimal and allows for incorrect device selection (HRM instead of Trainer).

ISS-0024.title: AI Features Not Restricted in Free Tier
ISS-0024.lead: AI Coach Analysis and AI Workout Generation features are currently accessible to Free tier users, which violates the monetization model.

ISS-0025.title: FTP Line Not Visible in Light Theme on Free Ride Screen
ISS-0025.lead: The FTP reference line on the Free Ride screen is not clearly visible when using the light theme, making it difficult for users to gauge their effort relative to their FTP.

ISS-0026.title: Favorites Are Global, Not Per-User
ISS-0026.lead: The isFavorite field is stored directly on the WorkoutProgram entity in the workout_programs table. This means: When one user favorites a workout, all users see it as favorited; Each rider cannot maintain their own list of favorite workouts; Conflicts with Family tier use case w…

ISS-0028.title: Strava Link in Global Settings Instead of User Profile
ISS-0028.lead: The Strava "Link Account" / "Unlink" control was placed in the generic application Settings screen (Settings → Connected Services). Since Strava is a per-rider connection, it is confusing to have it in a screen that is not rider-specific.

ISS-0029.title: Strava Shows Connected on Website but App Shows 'Not Connected'
ISS-0029.lead: After completing the OAuth flow (browser → Strava login → authorize → server redirect → app), Strava's website correctly shows "Your Trainer" as an authorized application. However, the app still displays "Not connected" and shows the "Link Account" button. The tokens are never p…

ISS-0030.title: Strava Workout Not Uploaded After Completion
ISS-0030.lead: After completing a workout, the FIT file is not automatically uploaded to Strava. The user's Strava account shows no new activity. The Strava upload feature requires the user to manually navigate to Workout History and tap an explicit upload button — this is not the expected beh…

ISS-0031.title: Strava Token Exchange Uses Wrong URL (api/v3/oauth/token vs oauth/token)
ISS-0031.lead: After completing the OAuth flow (browser → Strava login → authorize → server redirect → app deep link), the app correctly calls handleStravaAuth(code) but stravaApi.exchangeToken() throws an exception because it hits the wrong URL. The Strava account is never linked despite the…

ISS-0032.title: Strava Deep Link Creates New Activity Instance — User Lands on Rider Selection
ISS-0032.lead: After completing the Strava OAuth flow in the browser, the app opens but the user is taken to the Rider Selection screen instead of returning to the Rider Profile screen where they tapped "Link Account". After manually re-selecting their rider and navigating to preferences, Stra…

ISS-0033.title: Strava Link Not Persisting Across App Restarts
ISS-0033.lead: After successfully linking a Strava account (debug card confirms "OK — isStravaLinked=true") and closing the app completely, reopening the app shows "Not connected" for the Strava integration — even though the OAuth tokens were correctly saved to SharedPreferences.

ISS-0034.title: Strava Upload Status Not Displaying Correctly
ISS-0034.lead: After implementing upload status tracking (TASK-0084), the upload status UI does not work as expected. The user sees an upload error after a long wait, but there is no visibility into what went wrong — no logging exists in the upload pipeline to diagnose the failure point.

ISS-0035.title: Resistance Mode Gear 10 Initial Resistance Mismatch
ISS-0035.lead: When entering resistance mode, the initial resistance level is set to 25 (hardcoded in WorkoutViewModel.resetWorkout()), but gear 10's formula calculates ((10-1)/21)^2 * 100 = 18. This means the trainer receives resistance=25 on first entry, but if the user shifts to gear 9 and…

ISS-0036.title: FTP Test Missing Category/Difficulty and Wrong totalDuration
ISS-0036.lead: ftp_test.json is missing the category and difficulty fields that every other workout has. Additionally, totalDuration is set to 3600 but the intervals sum to 3120 (600+300+120+300+1200+600).

ISS-0037.title: Ramp Test Missing Difficulty Field
ISS-0037.lead: ramp_test.json has category: "Testing" but is missing the difficulty field. Every other workout file includes a difficulty rating.

ISS-0038.title: Sweet Spot Intervals Wrong totalDuration
ISS-0038.lead: sweet_spot.json has totalDuration: 1800 (30 min) but the intervals sum to 2100 (300+600+300+600+300 = 35 min). The code recalculates at load so runtime is correct, but the raw JSON is misleading.

ISS-0039.title: Sweet Spot 45 Filename Does Not Match 50-Min Content
ISS-0039.lead: File is named sweet_spot_45.json (suggesting 45 minutes), but the workout is actually 50 minutes (3000s). The programId is "sweet_spot_50" which is correct, but the filename is misleading.

ISS-0040.title: Pyramid Power 80% FTP Intervals Labeled Wrong Zone
ISS-0040.lead: In pyramid_power.json, the 80% FTP intervals (Steps 1 and 5 in both pyramid sets) are labeled Z2 (Endurance). At 80% FTP this is Tempo territory, which is Z3.

ISS-0041.title: Over-Under Intervals 105% FTP Labeled Wrong Zone
ISS-0041.lead: In over_unders.json, the "Over" intervals at 105% FTP are labeled Z4 (Threshold). At 105% FTP this crosses into VO2 Max territory, which is Z5.

ISS-0042.title: Restore Purchase Button Not Functional
ISS-0042.lead: The "Restore Purchase" button on the PaywallScreen calls onDismiss, which simply closes the paywall. It does not trigger any purchase restoration logic. Users who reinstall the app or switch devices have no manual way to recover their purchased entitlements.

ISS-0043.title: Stale PRO Tier After Purchase Revoke
ISS-0043.lead: After consuming/revoking a purchase via Developer Settings, the app continues to show PRO entitlements. The user cannot return to FREE tier without clearing app data.

ISS-0044.title: HRM Scanner Shows Trainer as Selectable Device
ISS-0044.lead: When scanning for a Heart Rate Monitor, the smart trainer appears in the device list. This happens because many trainers advertise both the FTMS service (0x1826) and the Heart Rate service (0x180D). The existing software filter only checked device names against a hardcoded list…

ISS-0045.title: Strava Linking Available on FREE Tier
ISS-0045.lead: FREE tier users can link their Strava account and trigger auto-uploads after workouts. Strava integration (linking, uploading, auto-upload) had no tier checks, unlike FIT export and CSV export which correctly require PRO/FAMILY.

ISS-0046.title: AI Coach Card Allows FREE Users to Submit Questions
ISS-0046.lead: The AI Coach card on the Workout History screen showed the question text field and Ask button to FREE users. Pressing Ask triggered the AI call, which then failed with a ProRequiredException and displayed an inline "Requires Pro or Family tier" error card with a "Go Pro" button.…

ISS-0047.title: AI Workout Builder Not Tier-Gated
ISS-0047.lead: The AI Workout Builder on the Create Workout screen allowed FREE users to type a prompt and click "Generate", which then failed with a ProRequiredException and displayed an inline error with a "Go Pro" button. Paid users with no API key configured could also type a prompt, click…

ISS-0048.lead: Google Play Console reports that the app targeting SDK 35 may not display correctly edge-to-edge on Android 15+. On Android 15, edge-to-edge is enforced by the system regardless, but without enableEdgeToEdge() the behavior is inconsistent across OS versions. The app manually set…

ISS-0049.title: Deprecated Edge-to-Edge APIs and Parameters
ISS-0049.lead: Google Play Console reports: "Your app uses deprecated APIs or parameters for edge-to-edge." On Android 15 (SDK 35), window.statusBarColor, window.navigationBarColor, and related theme attributes are deprecated and ignored. The app still referenced these through two paths: Manif…

ISS-0050.title: R8 Kotlin Metadata Parsing Warning
ISS-0050.lead: During release builds (isMinifyEnabled = true), R8 emits: WARNING: R8: An error occurred when parsing kotlin metadata. This normally happens when using a newer version of kotlin than the kotlin version released when this version of R8 was created.

ISS-0051.title: Missing .environment() in Sheet Presentations
ISS-0051.lead: SwiftUI .sheet() modifiers create independent view hierarchies that do NOT inherit @Environment objects from the presenting view. Views presented in sheets that use @Environment(MainViewModel.self), @Environment(BillingService.self), etc. will crash at runtime with a missing env…

ISS-0052.title: Strava Retry Uploads Empty Metrics
ISS-0052.lead: retryFailedUploads() in StravaService.swift iterates over sessions with stravaUploadStatus == "FAILED" but passes an empty metrics array [] to the upload function instead of fetching actual workout metrics from SwiftData.

ISS-0053.title: LicensingManager Passed as Nil to WorkoutViewModel
ISS-0053.lead: WorkoutViewModel.setup() accepts an optional licensingManager parameter. In the current app wiring (YourTrainerApp.swift), LicensingManager is not created or injected, so it defaults to nil. All licensing checks (custom workout limits, monthly reset) are silently skipped.

ISS-0054.title: SoundManager Creates New AVAudioEngine Per Play
ISS-0054.lead: SoundManager.play() creates a new AVAudioEngine and AVAudioPlayerNode for every sound. These are never explicitly stopped or detached after playback completes, leading to engine accumulation in memory during a workout with frequent interval transitions.

ISS-0055.title: Auto-Upload Does Not Set Session stravaUploadStatus
ISS-0055.lead: After a successful auto-upload to Strava in completeWorkout(), the session's stravaUploadStatus field is not updated to "UPLOADED". The persistent upload queue's retryFailedUploads() will find the session still in its old status and attempt to re-upload it.

ISS-0056.title: MainActor Violations in Observable ViewModels
ISS-0056.lead: Several @Observable view model methods that mutate published state are not annotated @MainActor. When called from async contexts (e.g., BLE callbacks, network completions), state mutations may occur on background threads, violating SwiftUI's requirement that view state changes h…

ISS-0057.title: Token Refresh Race Condition
ISS-0057.lead: When multiple async operations discover an expired Strava token simultaneously (e.g., auto-upload + retry queue), each will independently call refreshToken(). This causes concurrent refresh requests that may invalidate each other's tokens — the second refresh may use a refresh t…

ISS-0058.title: pendingSoundEffect State Set But Never Observed
ISS-0058.lead: WorkoutViewModel has a pendingSoundEffect published property that is set during interval transitions but is never read by any view. The actual sound playback goes through SoundManager.shared.play() directly. This is dead code that adds confusion.

ISS-0059.title: selectUser() Not @MainActor
ISS-0059.lead: MainViewModel.selectUser() modifies @Observable state (currentUserId, currentUserName, etc.) but is not annotated @MainActor. If called from a background context, this violates SwiftUI's thread safety requirements.

ISS-0060.title: Cadence Ramp Detection Has No Debounce
ISS-0060.lead: handleCadenceRamp() in WorkoutViewModel checks cadence against ramp thresholds on every BLE update (~1Hz for most sensors, sometimes faster). Rapid cadence fluctuations near a threshold boundary could trigger multiple ramp changes per second, causing erratic resistance changes.

ISS-0061.title: WorkoutEditorView Save May Not Persist to SwiftData
ISS-0061.lead: WorkoutEditorView calls onSave(workout) closure when saving, but the calling site must wire this to WorkoutRepository.saveCustomWorkout(). If the closure only updates in-memory state without persisting to SwiftData, custom workouts will be lost on app relaunch.

ISS-0062.title: Auto-Reconnect Timers Not Cancelled on disconnectAll()
ISS-0062.lead: disconnectAll() in BluetoothService disconnects peripherals and stops scanning but does not cancel any pending auto-reconnect timers. After disconnectAll(), a pending reconnect timer could fire and re-initiate a connection to a device the user explicitly disconnected.

ISS-0063.title: Auto-Upload Sets stravaUploadStatus Without context.save()
ISS-0063.lead: In ActiveWorkoutView.autoUploadToStrava(), session.stravaUploadStatus is set to "uploading", "uploaded", or "failed" but context.save() is never called. If the app crashes during upload, the status mutation is lost — the session reverts to its pre-upload state and the user has n…

ISS-0064.title: StravaService refreshTask Property Race Condition
ISS-0064.lead: StravaService.refreshTask is a mutable Task<String, Error>? property on a non-actor @Observable class. The coalescing logic in getValidAccessToken() reads and writes refreshTask without synchronization. If two concurrent calls to uploadSession() both need a token refresh, they c…

ISS-0065.title: KeychainRepository Ignores OSStatus Return Values
ISS-0065.lead: KeychainRepository.saveKey() calls SecItemAdd() on line 21 and discards the OSStatus return value. deleteKey() similarly discards the result of SecItemDelete(). If the Keychain is locked, full, or the app lacks entitlements, these operations silently fail and the caller has no w…

ISS-0066.title: WorkoutRepository Asset Loading Silently Returns Empty
ISS-0066.lead: In WorkoutRepository.loadAssetWorkouts(), if Bundle.main.url(forResource: "workouts", withExtension: nil) returns nil, the method silently returns an empty array. Users see no workouts and no error indication. Individual file decode failures are also silently skipped via try?.

ISS-0067.title: AddRiderSheet Accepts Invalid Weight Values
ISS-0067.lead: AddRiderSheet allows saving a rider with weight of 0, negative values, or extremely large values. The Save button is only disabled when the name is empty. Invalid weight causes incorrect W/kg calculations, FTP estimates, and physics simulations.

ISS-0068.title: StravaNetworkClient Uses Default URLSession Without Timeout Configuration
ISS-0068.lead: StravaNetworkClient uses URLSession.shared for all network requests. The default timeoutIntervalForRequest is 60 seconds and timeoutIntervalForResource is 7 days. For FIT file uploads on slow connections, the request timeout may be too short. For token exchange and refresh, the…

ISS-0069.title: Weight Conversion Constant Duplicated Across Files
ISS-0069.lead: The kg-to-lbs conversion constant 2.20462 appears in both FormattingProvider.formatWeight() and AddRiderSheet (init and onChange). If one is updated and the other isn't, they'll produce inconsistent results.

ISS-0100.title: WorkoutEditorView Sheet Missing LicensingManager Environment
ISS-0100.lead: FEAT-0036 TASK-0206 added @Environment(LicensingManager.self) to WorkoutEditorView so it can check the effective tier for custom workout limits. However, the .sheet() in WorkoutSelectionView that presents WorkoutEditorView did not pass the licensingManager environment — causing…

ISS-0105.title: Android: Strava FIT Upload Uses Session-Average Metrics Instead of Per-Second Points
ISS-0105.lead: iOS TASK-0198 fixed the Strava upload to fetch real per-second SessionMetricPoint records from SwiftData instead of constructing synthetic metrics from powerHistory with session-average HR/cadence. The equivalent issue exists in Android.

ISS-0107.title: Resume Workout button available after workout fully completed
ISS-0107.lead: When a workout completes (timer finishes all intervals or user manually ends via "End & Save"), the CompletionOverlay shows a "Resume Workout" button. For workouts that have fully completed (all intervals finished, isTimerFinished == true), resuming does not make sense — there a…

ISS-0108.title: First workout save for family rider may show paywall instead of export options
ISS-0108.lead: When saving the first workout for a non-primary rider on a Family license, the FIT Export and Strava upload options can sometimes be disabled and the paywall/license selection screen appears instead. This occurred once and was difficult to reproduce, suggesting a race condition…

ISS-0109.title: Strava Retry button can upload workouts using wrong rider's credentials
ISS-0109.lead: With 3 riders (Test = main rider with Strava, Test2 = second rider with Strava, Test3 = third rider without Strava), pressing the Strava Retry button can cause workouts from Test2 to appear on Test3's (or another rider's) view, or upload to the wrong Strava account.

ISS-0110.title: History shows only latest session after workout save
ISS-0110.lead: When completing a workout and navigating to the History screen, only the just-completed session is visible. Previously saved workouts for the current rider are missing. Navigating away and back to History shows all sessions correctly.

ISS-0111.title: ERG ramp transition has power discontinuity at interval boundaries
ISS-0111.lead: The ERG ramp smoothing logic in WorkoutMath.calculateTargetPower() has a progress formula that never reaches 1.0, creating a power jump at the point where the ramp-from-previous expires and the steady-state target takes over.

ISS-0112.title: Strava upload spinner persists indefinitely when WiFi is off
ISS-0112.lead: After completing a workout with WiFi off, the history screen shows "Uploading..." with a spinner. When WiFi is re-enabled, the upload succeeds silently — no error or retry was ever shown. The spinner stays until the upload completes.

ISS-0113.title: Non-Strava rider briefly shows 'not uploaded to strava' after save
ISS-0113.lead: When completing a workout as a rider who does NOT have Strava linked, the history screen briefly shows a Strava status message (e.g., "not uploaded to strava" or an upload option). Navigating away and back removes the message.

ISS-0114.title: FTP text field resets to default when cleared
ISS-0114.lead: When editing a rider's FTP in the profile screen, clearing the text field causes the previous/default value to immediately reappear. The user cannot clear the field to type a new value from scratch — the old value snaps back.

ISS-0115.title: ERG target power not updating on trainer (Elite Direto)
ISS-0115.lead: User reports that during an ERG workout, the trainer stays at ~100W (warm-up power) even after transitioning to higher-power intervals. The target power displayed in the UI updates correctly but the trainer's resistance doesn't change. In Free Ride mode, changing the bias percen…

ISS-0117.title: Incorrect cadence readings cause ERG power oscillation spikes
ISS-0117.lead: During a 60-minute Sweet Spot workout on an Elite Direto, the user reports: Cadence frequently shows incorrect values (e.g., 75 or 67 RPM when actually pedaling at 90 RPM); The incorrect cadence appears for a few seconds, then returns to correct; The problem worsens over time; T…

ISS-0118.title: No recovery path for mid-workout BLE connection failure
ISS-0118.lead: If a BLE device disconnects during an active workout, there is no way to reconnect without abandoning the workout.

ISS-0119.title: Inconsistent time display — missing segment elapsed/total and ETA
ISS-0119.lead: The cockpit shows: Workout: elapsed time and total time; Segment: only remaining time

ISS-0120.title: Metric values flicker between decimal and no-decimal format
ISS-0120.lead: During a workout, some metric values (calories and possibly others) alternate between showing a decimal point and not having one. For example, "595" then "595.2" then "596". This causes the number to shift position, which is visually distracting.

ISS-0121.title: Skipping back to repeat intervals discards recorded data and shortens session
ISS-0121.lead: User performed a 40/20 micro-intervals workout and wanted to extend it. After the mid-recovery, he pressed "Previous Section" repeatedly to return to the start of the intervals and did the set 3 times total. The workout took ~1.8 hours, but: Duration shows 47 min (the planned wo…

ISS-0122.title: Workout segments show no power or duration until workout starts
ISS-0122.lead: When browsing available workouts, the user can see the terrain profile graph but cannot see the target watts or duration for any segment. Navigating into a workout shows zero everywhere. Skipping forward still shows zero. The user has to actually start the workout before any num…

ISS-0123.title: Power labels only appear on first few terrain segments
ISS-0123.lead: User reports that the watt labels on the terrain graph only appear on the first few segments. Later segments in the workout show no power information, making it unclear what power target they'll be hitting.

ISS-0124.title: Need workout duration variants (30/60/90 min) and duration filtering
ISS-0124.lead: User prefers 60-minute workouts but most bundled workouts are 30-45 minutes. They use the skip-back feature to repeat intervals (which works well since ISS-0121), but would prefer dedicated 60/90-minute versions.

ISS-0125.title: Strava upload robustness — WiFi loss, re-upload, and edge cases
ISS-0125.lead: User reports never having seen a Strava upload fail, and asks about robustness in edge cases: What happens if WiFi is pulled during upload? What happens if the Strava event is deleted after upload? Can it be re-uploaded? How robust is the retry mechanism?

ISS-0126.title: Workout editor form is too cumbersome — users abandon it
ISS-0126.lead: User reports opening the custom workout editor, seeing the form-based interface, and abandoning it: "When I clicked into the form, I was met with disdain. The form looked a bit cumbersome, so I abandoned it and moved on."

ISS-0127.title: Rider card needs personal color for visual identity
ISS-0127.lead: In a Family household with multiple riders, the cards are visually similar — all use the same accent color for the icon and border (a tier-colour fallback existed in code but was unreachable, and would have meant multiple riders shared the same border anyway). Users need a way t…

ISS-0128.title: Rider card layout on profile settings page needs redesign
ISS-0128.lead: The rider card displayed at the top of the profile/settings page looks out of place with the current layout. The full portrait card takes up significant vertical space before the user reaches the settings fields.

ISS-0129.title: ERG mode minimum too high in free ride — cannot go below 50% FTP
ISS-0129.lead: In free ride mode with ERG enabled, the intensity cannot be lowered below 50% of FTP. For a 200W FTP rider this means 100W minimum — too high for easy warm-up, cool-down, or recovery spinning. Users expect to be able to dial down to very light resistance.

ISS-0130.lead: In resistance (manual) mode, the UI displays "GEAR 10" with a virtual shifting metaphor (gears 1-22 mapped quadratically to 0-100% resistance). Users expect to see a slope/gradient setting (e.g., "5% grade") because that's how real-world cycling and most competing apps present r…

ISS-0290.title: LTHR field on Rider Profile did not always re-derive when Max HR changed. Root cause was a race: the (then) un-debounced save effect persisted transient out-of-range Max HR values as `null` mid-typing, which re-emitted `currentUser`, which re-keyed `remember(currentUser)` and clobbered both the rider's in-progress input and the just-derived LTHR. Fixed 2026-06-08 with a 400ms debounce on the save effect plus removal of the LTHR derive effect's `currentUser.maxHeartRate` fallback (strict derivation from the field only).

TASK-0139.title: Fix MockBluetoothProvider Blocker
TASK-0139.lead: The app currently uses MockBluetoothProvider in the production code path. ScanViewModel is initialized with a mock provider, so real BLE hardware never connects.

TASK-0140.title: Add Bluetooth Permission Handling
TASK-0140.lead: The app is missing NSBluetoothAlwaysUsageDescription in Info.plist and has no runtime permission checks, causing CoreBluetooth to fail silently or crash.

TASK-0141.title: Implement BLE Auto-Reconnect
TASK-0141.lead: When a BLE device disconnects unexpectedly during a workout, the app makes no attempt to reconnect. Android retries 3 times with exponential backoff.

TASK-0142.title: Fix disconnectAll() No-Op
TASK-0142.lead: ScanViewModel.disconnectAll() has an empty body or doesn't actually disconnect peripherals. Called from SettingsView and navigation cleanup.

TASK-0143.title: Add Trainer Connection Gating
TASK-0143.lead: Users can start a workout without any trainer connected. Without a trainer, ERG mode writes go nowhere and no power/cadence data is received.

TASK-0144.title: Fix Strava OAuth Redirect Mismatch
TASK-0144.lead: Strava OAuth will never complete because the redirect URI and the ASWebAuthenticationSession callback scheme don't match.

TASK-0145.title: Fix FIT Encoder Base Types
TASK-0145.lead: FIT definition messages hardcode all field base types to 0 (ENUM), producing malformed files that Strava may reject.

TASK-0146.title: Move Strava Tokens to Keychain
TASK-0146.lead: Strava OAuth tokens are stored in UserDefaults, which is not encrypted. They should be in the iOS Keychain.

TASK-0147.title: Remove Hardcoded Strava Client Secret
TASK-0147.lead: StravaService.swift line 8 contains the Strava client secret in source code. Anyone decompiling the app binary can extract it.

TASK-0148.title: Strava Auto-Upload on Workout Save
TASK-0148.lead: Android automatically uploads to Strava when a workout is saved (if linked). iOS has no auto-upload trigger.

TASK-0149.title: Per-Session Strava Upload Buttons in History
TASK-0149.lead: Workout history shows stravaUploadStatus but has no interactive upload or retry buttons.

TASK-0150.title: Strava Persistent Upload Queue
TASK-0150.lead: Failed Strava uploads don't survive app restart. Android uses WorkManager for persistent retry.

TASK-0151.title: Fix WorkoutViewModel Timer Task Leak
TASK-0151.lead: WorkoutViewModel starts a Task { while true { ... } } for the workout timer but never stores or cancels it. If the user navigates away, the Task runs indefinitely.

TASK-0152.title: Fix saveSession() Error Handling
TASK-0152.lead: saveSession() uses try? for SwiftData inserts, silently losing workout data on failure.

TASK-0153.title: Fix resistanceForGear Rounding
TASK-0153.lead: resistanceForGear() uses Swift's .rounded() (round half to even) while Android uses toInt() (truncation). This produces a 1% divergence at gear 11.

TASK-0154.title: Add Workout Sound Effects
TASK-0154.lead: Android uses ToneGenerator for countdown beeps before interval transitions. iOS has a pendingSoundEffect property but never plays any audio.

TASK-0155.title: Keep Screen On During Workout
TASK-0155.lead: The screen dims and locks during active workouts, forcing the rider to unlock mid-ride. Android uses FLAG_KEEP_SCREEN_ON.

TASK-0156.title: Completion Overlay — Resume, Discard, Update FTP
TASK-0156.lead: The completion overlay only shows stats and "Done". Android provides Resume, Discard, Update FTP, and Share to Strava options.

TASK-0157.title: Active Workout Metric Sub-Values and Polish
TASK-0157.lead: Several cockpit metric features from Android are missing.

TASK-0158.title: WorkoutViewModel Missing CRUD Methods
TASK-0158.lead: WorkoutViewModel is missing several methods present in the Android WorkoutViewModel.

TASK-0159.title: Custom Workout Create, Edit, Import, Export
TASK-0159.lead: Android has a full custom workout pipeline (WorkoutEditorScreen) that is completely missing from iOS.

TASK-0160.title: Refactor Service Wiring — Fix ViewModel Scoping
TASK-0160.lead: ViewModels are created as @State inside RiderSelectionView, causing them to be re-created on every view re-render and not shared across the navigation stack.

TASK-0161.title: Enforce Rider Limit on addUser()
TASK-0161.lead: MainViewModel.addUser() creates riders without checking tier limits. FREE users should be limited to 1 rider, FAMILY to 6.

TASK-0162.title: Edit Rider Profile from Rider Card
TASK-0162.lead: Android allows editing a rider's profile from the rider card. iOS only supports Delete via long-press context menu.

TASK-0163.title: Fix Paywall — Use Dynamic StoreKit Pricing
TASK-0163.lead: PaywallSheet hardcodes "$29.99" and "$49.99". Apple requires showing actual StoreKit prices.

TASK-0164.title: Fix Weight Label and Unit Conversion
TASK-0164.lead: Weight label always shows "kg" regardless of unit system selection. Value doesn't convert on toggle.

TASK-0165.title: Add About/Privacy Screen and Developer Settings
TASK-0165.lead: Missing About screen (required for App Store), privacy policy link, and developer settings.

TASK-0166.title: Family Tier Rank Ribbon on Rider Cards
TASK-0166.lead: Android shows a colored rank ribbon on rider cards for Family tier users.

TASK-0167.title: AI Coach and AI Workout Builder Placeholder Screens
TASK-0167.lead: Android has navigation entries and placeholder screens for AI Coach and AI Workout Builder. iOS should match for feature parity.

TASK-0168.title: MetricRepository Batch Delete
TASK-0168.lead: MetricRepository deletes metric points one at a time with individual saves, making session deletion O(n) — slow for long workouts.

TASK-0169.title: Fix WorkoutRepository Thread Safety
TASK-0169.lead: WorkoutRepository uses lazy var for the decoded workout list from JSON assets. lazy var is not thread-safe in Swift.

TASK-0170.title: Improve Data Layer Reactivity
TASK-0170.lead: Android uses Kotlin Flow for reactive data streams. iOS currently requires manual loadUsers() / loadWorkouts() calls after mutations. Data changes don't automatically reflect in the UI.

TASK-0171.title: Fix LicensingManager Monthly Reset Edge Cases
TASK-0171.lead: LicensingManager tracks ERG session usage per month using separate last_reset_month and last_reset_year UserDefaults integers. Edge cases exist around timezone changes and clock manipulation.

TASK-0173.title: Fix Strava Retry to Include Actual Workout Metrics

TASK-0174.title: Wire LicensingManager into App Environment

TASK-0176.lead: After successful auto-upload, session status is not updated, causing duplicate uploads.

TASK-0177.lead: Observable view models mutate state off the main actor in some code paths.

TASK-0179.lead: pendingSoundEffect property is set but never observed by any view.

TASK-0180.title: Add @MainActor to selectUser()

TASK-0181.lead: Cadence ramp detection fires on every BLE update, causing erratic resistance changes near threshold boundaries.

TASK-0182.title: Wire WorkoutEditorView Save to SwiftData Persistence
TASK-0182.lead: WorkoutEditorView's onSave closure may not persist to SwiftData.

TASK-0183.title: Cancel Reconnect Timers on disconnectAll()
TASK-0183.lead: Pending auto-reconnect timers are not cancelled when disconnectAll() is called.

TASK-0197.title: Wire BillingService into LicensingManager

TASK-0198.title: Fix Strava Upload to Use Actual Per-Second Metrics

TASK-0204.title: Fix timerTask deinit Safety in WorkoutViewModel
TASK-0204.lead: No data race on timerTask between deinit and MainActor methods.

TASK-0205.title: Fix retryFailedUploads MainActor Isolation
TASK-0205.lead: All SwiftData @Model property access happens on MainActor. No runtime crashes from off-actor model access.

TASK-0206.title: Allow FREE Tier to Create Up to 3 Custom Workouts
TASK-0206.lead: FREE tier users can create up to 3 custom workouts. Paywall shown when trying to create a 4th. PRO/FAMILY tier has no limit.

TASK-0207.title: Show Effective Tier in SettingsView

TASK-0208.title: Log MainViewModel context.save() Errors
TASK-0208.lead: All try? context.save() calls in MainViewModel replaced with do/catch + print().

TASK-0209.title: Cache DateFormatter in FormattingProvider
TASK-0209.lead: DateFormatter instance is a static let, not created per call.

TASK-0210.title: Fix PowerGraphView ForEach Non-Unique IDs

TASK-0211.title: Add Database Index to SessionMetricPoint.sessionId

REQ-0001.title: Device Connection (US-1)
REQ-0001.lead: As a cyclist, I want the app to automatically connect to my Wahoo KICKR Core and Whoop heart rate monitor via Bluetooth, so I can start training without manual device configuration.

REQ-0002.title: User Selection (US-2)
REQ-0002.lead: As a household member, I want to select my user profile which includes my personal FTP value, so workouts are calibrated to my fitness level.

REQ-0003.title: Workout Selection (US-3)
REQ-0003.lead: As a cyclist, I want to browse and select from pre-defined workout programs, so I can choose training sessions that match my goals.

REQ-0004.title: Visual Workout Display (US-4)
REQ-0004.lead: As a cyclist, I want to see the complete workout program displayed vertically with color-coded intensity zones, so I can preview the session structure before starting.

REQ-0005.title: Automated Resistance Control (US-5)
REQ-0005.lead: As a cyclist, I want the app to automatically adjust the trainer resistance according to the workout program, so I can focus on maintaining effort without manual adjustments.

REQ-0006.title: Real-Time Metrics (US-6)
REQ-0006.lead: As a cyclist, I want to see current power (watts), heart rate, cadence (RPM), elapsed time, and remaining time during the workout, so I can monitor my performance.

REQ-0007.title: Heart Rate Visualization (US-7)
REQ-0007.lead: As a cyclist, I want to see my current heart rate displayed as a color (blue to red gradient based on intensity), so I can quickly gauge my cardiovascular effort.

REQ-0008.title: Workout Completion (US-8)
REQ-0008.lead: As a cyclist, I want to see summary statistics (average heart rate, average power, etc.) at the end of the workout, so I can review my performance.

REQ-0009.title: Data Persistence (US-9)
REQ-0009.lead: As a cyclist, I want my completed workouts to be saved, so I can track progress over time.

REQ-0010.title: Workout Management (US-10)
REQ-0010.lead: As a cyclist, I want to create, edit, duplicate, and delete custom workout sessions, so I can build my own training library.

REQ-0011.title: Favoriting (US-11)
REQ-0011.lead: As a cyclist, I want to star my favorite workouts so they are always prioritized at the top of the selection list.

REQ-0012.title: Training Analytics (US-12)
REQ-0012.lead: As a rider, I want to see a visual summary of my lifetime training statistics (sessions, time, energy) on the history page.

REQ-0013.title: Screen Continuity (US-13)
REQ-0013.lead: As a user, I want my tablet screen to stay on for the entire duration of my workout without me having to touch it.

REQ-0014.title: Launch Compliance
REQ-0014.lead: Requirements for Google Play Store publication.

REQ-0015.title: Equipment Status Screen
REQ-0015.lead: As a rider, I want to confirm my trainer and heart rate monitor are connected after I select my profile, so I can be sure my data is being recorded correctly.

REQ-0016.title: Device Selection Screen
REQ-0016.lead: As a user, I want to scan and select a specific device when setting up for the first time or changing equipment.

REQ-0017.title: Rider Weight & Units
REQ-0017.lead: As a rider, I want to enter my weight so that I can see weight-adjusted metrics (W/kg) and have accurate metadata for my history.

REQ-0018.title: Energy Calculation Logic
REQ-0018.lead: As a rider, I want the system to calculate my energy expenditure accurately based on my power output.

REQ-0019.title: Energy & W/kg UI
REQ-0019.lead: As a rider, I want to see my calories burned and power-to-weight ratio during and after my ride.

REQ-0020.title: Workout Export (Share Intent)
REQ-0020.lead: As a rider, I want to send my custom workouts to my friends or save them to my cloud storage using standard Android apps.

REQ-0021.title: Workout File Import
REQ-0021.lead: As a rider, I want to import workout files shared by others into my training library, including Zwift .zwo workout files.

REQ-0022.title: File Association (.ytw)
REQ-0022.lead: "App registers an Intent Filter for .ytw (Your Trainer Workout) files."; "Tapping an .ytw file in a File Manager or Email launches Your Trainer."; "The import logic correctly parses the file content even when launched from an external Uri."

REQ-0023.title: AI Prompting Interface
REQ-0023.lead: As a rider, I want to describe my training goals in plain English and select my preferred AI engine to build the session for me.

REQ-0024.title: LLM Schema Context
REQ-0024.lead: The system must provide the LLM with enough structure to ensure the generated output is immediately usable by the WorkoutEngine.

REQ-0025.title: AI Response Validation & Import
REQ-0025.lead: The app must verify that the AI's 'hallucinations' don't break the workout engine or create dangerous training loads.

REQ-0026.title: Workout History CSV Export
REQ-0026.lead: As a rider, I want to export my full training history to Excel/CSV so I can perform my own analysis or back up my data.

REQ-0028.title: Secure API Key Storage (BYOK)
REQ-0028.lead: As a Pro user, I want to securely store multiple AI API keys so I can switch between different training partners.

REQ-0029.title: Pro Unlock Logic
REQ-0029.lead: As a developer, I want to monetize the app using standard Google Play In-App Purchases to comply with store policies.

REQ-0030.title: FIT File Export
REQ-0030.lead: As a Pro user, I want to export my ride data in the industry-standard .FIT format so I can upload it to any analysis platform.

REQ-0031.title: Strava Direct Upload
REQ-0031.lead: As a Pro user, I want my ride to automatically appear on Strava so I don't have to manually email files to myself.

REQ-0032.title: Dark Mode Toggle
REQ-0032.lead: As a user riding in a dimly lit pain cave, I want to force Dark Mode so the screen doesn't blind me.

REQ-0033.title: Accent Color Selection
REQ-0033.lead: As a user, I want to match the app's look to my bike or kit.

REQ-0034.title: Owner Identity & Family Logic
REQ-0034.lead: As a Family Pro user, I want to create separate profiles for my spouse and kids so our stats don't get mixed up.

REQ-0035.title: Smart ERG Transition Smoothing
REQ-0035.lead: As a rider, I want smooth transitions between resistance levels so my knees don't get slammed by sudden wattage jumps.

REQ-0036.title: FTP Ramp Test Protocol
REQ-0036.lead: As a rider, I want to accurately measure my fitness (FTP) without pacing a 20-minute time trial, so my training zones are correct.

REQ-0037.title: Manual Resistance (Sim Mode)
REQ-0037.lead: As a rider, I want to control the resistance manually (like changing gears) so I can pace myself during an FTP test or free ride.

REQ-0038.title: Virtual Shifting UI
REQ-0038.lead: As a rider, I need reachable buttons to adjust the difficulty up or down mid-ride.

REQ-0039.title: Time-Series Data Capture
REQ-0039.lead: As a data-driven athlete, I want 1-second resolution of my training data so I can analyze my power curve and interval execution.

REQ-0040.title: Free-Ride Session Profile Graph
REQ-0040.lead: As a rider performing an unstructured ride, I want to see a visual summary of my entire effort and how it relates to my FTP.

REQ-0041.title: Virtual Distance Calculation
REQ-0041.lead: As a rider, I want to see my virtual distance traveled during an indoor session so that I can track my progress and compare efforts on leaderboards.

REQ-0042.title: Local Data Sovereignty
REQ-0042.lead: As a privacy-conscious user, I want my training data to stay on my device so that my personal fitness information is never shared or stored on a central server.

REQ-0043.title: AI History Context
REQ-0043.lead: As a data-driven athlete, I want to query my training history using natural language so I can get insights without manually analyzing spreadsheets.

REQ-0044.title: Localization & Unit System Support
REQ-0044.lead: As a global user, I want the app to display data in my preferred unit system and regional format so that metrics are intuitive and easy to read.

REQ-0045.title: Watt/kg Visibility
REQ-0045.lead: As a competitive cyclist, I want W/kg to be prominent throughout the app so I can compare my performance relative to my weight and other riders.

REQ-0046.title: ERG Session Token Logic (retired 2026-06-09 under FEAT-0096 M1 — the 3-rides-per-month cap on FREE-tier riders was removed; FREE riders now ride bundled-allowlist workouts unlimited and locked workouts route per-tap to the paywall)
REQ-0046.lead: As a business owner, I want to provide a limited taste of automated training to free users while protecting the premium value of the ERG engine.

REQ-0047.title: Multi-Provider REST Configuration
REQ-0047.lead: The application must handle provider-specific networking configurations to communicate with external LLM services directly using user-provided credentials.

REQ-0048.title: Billing Debug Tools
REQ-0048.lead: As a developer and tester, I want to manually override my purchase status so I can verify Pro features without making real purchases.

REQ-0049.title: Google Play Promo Code Support
REQ-0049.lead: As a product manager, I want to distribute free Pro access to select influencers and beta testers using Google Play Promo Codes.

REQ-0050.title: Reactive Licensing State
REQ-0050.lead: The application must reactively update its capabilities and UI elements immediately upon a license state change, without requiring an app restart.

REQ-0051.title: Startup Failure Fallback
REQ-0051.lead: As a user, I want the app to handle internal initialization errors gracefully so I am informed of issues rather than experiencing a silent crash.

REQ-0052.title: Energy Terminology Clarity
REQ-0052.lead: To reduce confusion between metabolic expenditure and mechanical output, the system must use distinct terminology for each metric.

REQ-0053.title: Interval Transition Warning
REQ-0053.lead: To prepare riders for upcoming intensity changes, the system must provide a visual warning during the final seconds of an interval.

REQ-0054.title: Cadence Targets & Visualization
REQ-0054.lead: The system must support specific cadence objectives to help riders train for different terrain types (e.g., low-cadence climbing, high-cadence sprinting).

REQ-0055.title: Cadence Compliance & ERG Safety
REQ-0055.lead: The system must monitor rider cadence relative to targets and intervene during dangerous ERG-mode scenarios.

REQ-0056.title: Family Demo Data Injection
REQ-0056.lead: The system must provide a debug utility to inject a realistic family profile set into the local database to facilitate testing and screenshot generation for the Play Store.

REQ-0057.title: Tablet Split-Screen Support
REQ-0057.lead: Your Trainer must fully support Android's multi-window / split-screen mode on tablets. This is a key differentiator: riders can watch video content (race footage, music, virtual courses) alongside the live workout dashboard.

REQ-0058.title: Billing Library v7 Migration
REQ-0058.lead: The app currently uses billing-ktx:6.0.1. Google requires new apps to use Billing Library v7+ which introduces breaking API changes. The migration must be completed before production release.

REQ-0059.title: Ramp Interval Support
REQ-0059.lead: The YTW workout format must support ramp intervals where power transitions linearly from a start value to an end value over the interval duration.

REQ-0060.title: Coaching Text Events
REQ-0060.lead: The YTW workout format must support timed text events (coaching cues) within intervals, displayed on screen during an active workout session.

REQ-0061.title: Repeat Group Compression
REQ-0061.lead: The YTW workout format should support grouping intervals with a repeat count, allowing compact representation of repeating on/off patterns without expanding every interval individually.

REQ-0062.title: Published YTW JSON Schema
REQ-0062.lead: The .ytw workout file format must have a published JSON Schema specification that enables third-party tools and coaches to create valid workout files without reverse-engineering the app.

REQ-0063.title: ZWO Workout Import
REQ-0063.lead: The app must be able to import Zwift .zwo workout files and convert them to the internal WorkoutProgram format, unlocking thousands of existing community workouts for Your Trainer users.

REQ-0064.title: Weekly Training Trend Display
REQ-0064.lead: The workout history screen must display stat cards showing this week's training metrics (rides, hours, distance, work) alongside lifetime totals, with trend arrows comparing the current week to the rolling 4-week average of completed weeks.

REQ-0065.title: 28-Day Activity Bar Chart
REQ-0065.lead: The workout history screen must display a 28-day activity bar chart at the top, showing one bar per day for the last 4 weeks. Users must be able to toggle between Duration (minutes) and Energy (kJ or kcal) modes via a segmented button. Rest days appear as zero-height gaps. Today…

REQ-0066.title: Max Heart Rate Profile Setting
REQ-0066.lead: Each rider profile must include a max heart rate value (bpm) used for HR zone calculation. The rider should be able to manually enter their max HR on the profile settings page. If a birthYear is available, an age-based estimate (220 - age) should be shown as the default. If neit…

REQ-0067.title: Heart Rate Zone Time Calculation
REQ-0067.lead: When a workout is saved, the system must calculate time spent in each of 5 heart rate zones using the rider's max HR and the recorded HR metric points. Zone times must be stored on the WorkoutSession and displayed as colored horizontal bars in the workout history detail view.

REQ-0068.title: Adaptive Rider Card Scaling
REQ-0068.lead: The RiderCard composable must scale all visual properties (font sizes, padding, icon sizes, spacer heights, rating badge size) proportionally based on actual card dimensions, and must switch the attribute layout orientation based on a height threshold.

REQ-0069.title: Bike Icon Selection
REQ-0069.lead: The system must provide each rider with a selection of 8 bicycle-style icons for their rider card. All custom icons must be single-color vector drawables in a consistent minimal style, tinted with the rider's chosen color. The selection must persist per rider.

REQ-0070.title: Unified Premium Feature Gating
REQ-0070.lead: All tier-gated UI elements must use a consistent lock-icon pattern as defined in ADR-0009. FREE users must never be able to interact with a premium feature before seeing the gating indicator. Features requiring external configuration (BYOK API keys) must implement the three-stat…

REQ-0071.title: Session Metrics UI
REQ-0071.lead: As a rider, I want to see Normalized Power, TSS, Intensity Factor, and Variability Index on the session detail screen so I can evaluate workout quality without exporting data.

REQ-0072.title: Power Deviation Display
REQ-0072.lead: As a rider in resistance mode, I want to see how far my current power is from the interval's target so I can adjust my effort without ERG assistance.

REQ-0073.title: Configurable Power Smoothing
REQ-0073.lead: As a rider, I want to configure how many seconds my power reading is averaged over so I can see a stable number instead of noisy second-by-second fluctuations.

REQ-0074.title: Course Data Model
REQ-0074.lead: As a developer, I need a structured data model for terrain courses so the app can store, load, and render elevation profiles with distance and grade data.

REQ-0075.title: GPX/TCX Course Import
REQ-0075.lead: As a rider, I want to import a GPX or TCX file from a real-world route so I can ride that terrain on my indoor trainer.

REQ-0076.title: Terrain Elevation Visualization
REQ-0076.lead: As a rider, I want to see the full terrain profile as an elevation silhouette with my current position so I can anticipate upcoming climbs and descents.

REQ-0077.title: Grade-Based Resistance Simulation
REQ-0077.lead: As a rider, I want the trainer's resistance to change based on the terrain gradient so riding a course feels like riding outdoors — harder on climbs, easier on descents.

REQ-0078.title: Ghost Rider System
REQ-0078.lead: As a rider, I want to race against my previous best lap on a course, and against family members' best laps, so I can track improvement and compete lap by lap.

REQ-0079.title: Course Tier Gating
REQ-0079.lead: As a product owner, I want course rides to share the existing free-tier session limit and ghost racing to require Pro/Family so the feature drives upgrades while remaining accessible.

REQ-0080.title: AI Course Generation
REQ-0080.lead: As a rider, I want to describe a course in natural language and have the AI generate a terrain profile so I can ride custom courses without needing a GPX file.

REQ-0081.title: Workout Loop Control
REQ-0081.lead: The active workout screen must provide a repeat button that allows riders to set 1, 2, 3, or unlimited (∞) extra repeats of the body intervals. Only body intervals loop (warmup plays once, cooldown plays after the last pass — except when ∞ is selected, in which case the ride end…

REQ-0082.title: Continuous Session Recording Across Loops
REQ-0082.lead: When a workout is looped, the session recording must capture the entire ride as a single continuous session. Duration, power history, and analytics span all loops.

REQ-0083.title: Real-time Zone Duration Timer
REQ-0083.lead: The system shall display a real-time timer showing how long the rider's heart rate has been continuously within the target HR zone during HR Zone Lock free ride mode. A secondary metric shall show the cumulative total time spent in the target zone for the entire session.

REQ-0084.title: Zone Segment Averages
REQ-0084.lead: While the rider's heart rate is within the target HR zone during HR Zone Lock free ride mode, the cockpit shall display average HR, average power, and average cadence for the current continuous zone segment, replacing the session-wide AVG/MAX statistics.

REQ-0085.title: HR Overlay Rendering
REQ-0085.lead: As a rider, I want to see my heart rate trace overlaid on the workout profile so I can correlate cardiac response with power output and terrain.

REQ-0090.title: Course Sharing & Ghost Import/Export
REQ-0090.lead: As a rider, I want to share a completed course ride with another rider so they can ride the same course and race against my performance as a ghost.

REQ-0091.title: History Session Thumbnails
REQ-0091.lead: As a rider, I want to visually distinguish structured workout sessions from course ride sessions in my workout history so I can quickly identify what type of ride each entry represents.

REQ-0092.title: Community Sync Protocol & Client
REQ-0092.lead: As a rider in a cycling group, I want my app to automatically sync course ghost data with a group-managed server or cloud folder so I can see a leaderboard and race against my training partners.

REQ-0093.title: Course Leaderboard UI
REQ-0093.lead: As a rider, I want to see a ranked leaderboard of best lap times for each course so I can compare my performance against my training partners and set competitive goals.

REQ-0101.lead: Superseded by PHASE-019 / FEAT-0098 (recorded 2026-07-24). Its implementing feature FEAT-0032 was superseded on 2026-06-14 and its scope absorbed into docs/features/ios-parity/PARITY_MATRIX.md; PHASE-019 § "Baseline reconciliation" treats the PHASE-012 hardening requirements as…

REQ-0102.lead: Superseded by PHASE-019 / FEAT-0098 (recorded 2026-07-24). Its implementing feature FEAT-0032 was superseded on 2026-06-14 and its scope absorbed into docs/features/ios-parity/PARITY_MATRIX.md; PHASE-019 § "Baseline reconciliation" treats the PHASE-012 hardening requirements as…

REQ-0103.lead: Superseded by PHASE-019 / FEAT-0098 (recorded 2026-07-24). Its implementing feature FEAT-0033 was superseded on 2026-06-14 and its scope absorbed into docs/features/ios-parity/PARITY_MATRIX.md; PHASE-019 § "Baseline reconciliation" treats the PHASE-012 hardening requirements as…

REQ-0104.title: iOS Environment Propagation in Sheets
REQ-0104.lead: All SwiftUI .sheet() modifiers in the iOS app must explicitly pass @Environment objects (MainViewModel, BillingService, StravaService, ScanViewModel, WorkoutViewModel) to presented views. SwiftUI sheets create independent view hierarchies that do not inherit environment from the…

REQ-0105.title: iOS Concurrency Safety
REQ-0105.lead: All mutations of @Observable state in iOS view models must occur on the main actor. Async operations that access shared mutable state (e.g., token refresh) must be serialized to prevent data races.

REQ-0106.title: iOS Data Persistence Integrity
REQ-0106.lead: All mutations to persisted state (SwiftData models, Keychain entries) must be explicitly saved/committed and their success or failure must be observable. Silent data loss from unsaved mutations or ignored error codes is not acceptable.

REQ-0107.lead: Superseded by PHASE-019 / FEAT-0098 (recorded 2026-07-24). Its implementing feature FEAT-0036 was superseded on 2026-06-14 and its scope absorbed into docs/features/ios-parity/PARITY_MATRIX.md; PHASE-019 § "Baseline reconciliation" treats the PHASE-012 hardening requirements as…
