REQ-0108.lead: Superseded by PHASE-019 / FEAT-0098 (recorded 2026-07-24). Its implementing feature FEAT-0036 was superseded on 2026-06-14 and its scope absorbed into docs/features/ios-parity/PARITY_MATRIX.md; PHASE-019 § "Baseline reconciliation" treats the PHASE-012 hardening requirements as…

REQ-0109.title: Backup Status Indicator
REQ-0109.lead: The Settings screen shall include a Data Backup section with clear user-facing copy about what happens to user data on uninstall, factory reset, or device swap — paired with a deep link to Android's backup settings so the user can verify and change the state themselves.

REQ-0110.title: Backup File Format
REQ-0110.lead: Exported backups shall be gzip-framed, versioned JSON files that capture the full restorable state of the device while excluding credentials and transient data. Gzip framing keeps the file inspectable (gunzip + any JSON tool) while cutting size by ~90% on metric-point-heavy payl…

REQ-0111.title: Backup Export & Import
REQ-0111.lead: The app shall expose user-initiated Export Backup and Import Backup actions from the Settings screen. Export writes the REQ-0110 file format to a user-chosen location. Import reads a file of that format and restores device state.

REQ-0112.title: Android Auto Backup Configuration
REQ-0112.lead: The app shall configure Android Auto Backup to silently protect user training data while explicitly excluding credentials and transient files. This provides a safety net for users who have device backup enabled, independent of the manual export flow.

REQ-0113.title: Workout Type Tabs on Selection Screen
REQ-0113.lead: The Workout Selection screen shall present three peer tabs — Power, Route, and Heart Rate — each with a Free Ride entry and a library of structured workouts of that type.

REQ-0114.title: Unified WorkoutProgram Schema with Type Discriminator
REQ-0114.lead: WorkoutProgram shall support all three workout types in a single table, discriminated by a workout-level workoutType field. Intervals carry nullable type-specific fields; intervals do not carry a type discriminator of their own — they inherit their type from the parent workout.

REQ-0115.title: HR-Zone Workout Type
REQ-0115.lead: Structured HR-Zone workouts shall drive the existing HR Zone-Lock algorithm from interval-level zone targets. The rider follows the workout's target zone over time; the algorithm adjusts power to keep HR in zone, same mechanism as FEAT-0044.

REQ-0116.title: Route Workout Type
REQ-0116.lead: Structured Route workouts shall drive trainer simulation mode from grade values interpolated from a routeProfile (list of distance+elevation points stored on WorkoutProgram). Progress through the route is measured in distance (from the physics engine), not wall-clock time. Virtu…

REQ-0117.title: Route Import Formats (GPX, FIT Course, TCX)
REQ-0117.lead: Route workouts shall be importable from the three common industry formats: GPX, FIT Course, and TCX. Trackpoint elevation data shall be smoothed for GPS noise and stored as a routeProfile on the workout — the full elevation profile is preserved, not segmented into intervals.

REQ-0118.title: Route Editor (Parametric)
REQ-0118.lead: Users shall be able to author Route workouts via a parametric segment editor. Each segment is defined by length and average grade. The editor shows a live elevation preview but does not offer map-based or draw-elevation modes.

REQ-0119.title: HR-Zone Workout Editor
REQ-0119.lead: Users shall be able to author HR-Zone workouts via a structured editor analogous to the Visual Workout Builder but with target zone selectors instead of power sliders.

REQ-0120.title: HR-Zone Algorithm Presets
REQ-0120.lead: The HR Zone-Lock algorithm shall expose three named parameter presets tuned for different training intents, selectable per workout, per interval, or live at ride time.

REQ-0121.title: Capture Free Ride as Workout
REQ-0121.lead: The app shall capture the rider's intensity inputs during Free Ride in any of the three domains and let the rider convert the captured timeline into a saved structured workout of that domain. Primary use case is Route (slope inputs become an elevation profile); Power and HR-Zone…

REQ-0122.title: Workout History Type Filter
REQ-0122.lead: The Workout History screen shall let users filter past sessions by workout type and shall display each session's type prominently.

REQ-0123.title: Default Workout Type (Last-Used Memory)
REQ-0123.lead: The Workout Selection screen shall open to whichever workout-type tab the current rider last used, to minimize friction for riders who mostly stick to one domain.

REQ-0124.title: Workout Type Premium Gating
REQ-0124.lead: Gating extends the existing Freemium model (REQ-0027) to cover all three workout domains uniformly. Free Ride remains free and unconstrained in every domain — this preserves the "lightweight FTMS controller" positioning the app is valued for. Structured workouts share a single m…

REQ-0125.title: Route Export Format (.ytroute) — CLOSED: superseded by unified .ytw
REQ-0125.lead: Route workouts shall export to a purpose-built .ytroute JSON format. This format is lossless for the internal Route representation (segments of {distanceMeters, targetGradePercent}) and is distinct from .ytw (which stays Power-only).

REQ-0126.title: HR-Zone Workout File Format (.ythr) — CLOSED: superseded by unified .ytw
REQ-0126.lead: HR-Zone workouts shall use a purpose-built .ythr JSON format for import and export. No industry standard exists for HR-zone-targeted interval workouts, so the format is defined here.

REQ-0127.title: Per-Rider File Format (.ytrider.json.gz)
REQ-0127.lead: Per-rider exports use a purpose-built file format distinct from the device-level backup format from FEAT-0047. The file carries exactly one rider's data with a clean separation of concerns.

REQ-0128.title: Per-Rider Export
REQ-0128.lead: From Settings, the user shall be able to pick a rider on-device and export that rider's complete session history and profile to a .ytrider.json.gz file.

REQ-0129.title: Per-Rider Import Dispatch
REQ-0129.lead: When importing a .ytrider.json.gz file, the receiving device shall not silently clobber existing data. The user shall choose between two distinct outcomes, both executed atomically inside a single Room transaction.

REQ-0130.title: Personal Best Metric Definitions (per domain)
REQ-0130.lead: Each of the three workout domains shall define a single primary PB metric with lower-is-better or higher-is-better semantics, plus a fixed set of secondary metrics shown alongside for context. The primary metric determines PB ordering; secondary metrics are display-only.

REQ-0131.title: A new personal best is the celebration's headline, with the comparison under it
REQ-0131.lead: When a saved ride sets a new personal best on a structured workout or route, the celebration after Save shall say so in its headline, New best on <name>. The best's value shall be the large number under the headline, and one line under that shall say by how much it beat the prev…

REQ-0132.title: Personal Best Badges in Library & History
REQ-0132.lead: The rider shall see their personal-best attempts surfaced in three places: the workout library (per workout), the history screen (per session that set a PB), and the workout detail screen (full attempts list).

REQ-0133.title: PB Validity Thresholds & Tie-Break Rules
REQ-0133.lead: A session shall qualify as a PB candidate only when it meets the validity thresholds defined below. When two qualifying attempts are equal within tolerance, the tie-break ordering shall be deterministic.

REQ-0134.title: Per-Rider PB Scope
REQ-0134.lead: Personal bests shall be computed and stored per rider. Different riders on the same device maintain independent PB records for the same workout. Household / family-aggregated PBs are out of scope for v1.

REQ-0135.title: HR-Zone Sensitivity Matrix — cadence × step magnitude
REQ-0135.lead: Define the two-axis configuration model that drives HR-Zone-Lock controller behaviour, replacing the current hardcoded values. Up-direction and down-direction values are each expressible separately, but the presets keep the asymmetric shape (down always ≤ up).

REQ-0136.lead: The HrZoneTrackingConfig (REQ-0135) must persist on the rider profile (not the device or the app-wide settings), survive backup/restore, and be adjustable through a tuning screen that also offers a single "Reset to default" action.

REQ-0139.title: Custom Photo Avatar
REQ-0139.lead: The system should allow a rider to upload a personal photo as their rider card icon. The photo must be displayed as a circle-cropped image and must gracefully fall back to the bike icon if the photo becomes unavailable.

REQ-0140.title: Configurable HR Zone Boundaries
REQ-0140.lead: The system must allow each rider to configure their own HR zone boundaries. The default must match the current fixed 5-zone model. Custom boundaries must be used for both real-time zone display and post-workout zone time computation.

REQ-0141.title: Real-time HR Zone Display
REQ-0141.lead: The active workout screen must display the rider's current HR zone next to the heart rate value, color-coded by zone intensity. The zone must update in real-time and use the rider's configured zone boundaries.

REQ-0142.title: HR Zone Target Free Ride
REQ-0142.lead: Free ride mode should allow the rider to select a target HR zone. The system must display the zone's HR boundaries and provide visual feedback on whether the rider's current HR is below, within, or above the target zone. This is informational only — no automatic resistance adjus…

REQ-0143.title: HR Zone-Lock Control Algorithm
REQ-0143.lead: The system must implement a PID-style control algorithm that automatically adjusts ERG target power to keep the rider's heart rate within a selected zone. The algorithm must be stable (no oscillation), responsive (converge within 2-3 minutes), and safe (bounded power output).

REQ-0144.title: HR Zone-Lock Safety
REQ-0144.lead: The HR zone-lock mode must handle sensor failures, data anomalies, and user override safely. The system must never produce dangerous power targets due to sensor dropout or noisy data.

REQ-0145.title: Simulation Mode Controls
REQ-0145.lead: The system must replace the current ERG / Resistance toggle with an ERG / Simulation toggle. Simulation mode retires the standalone Resistance mode — virtual gears (1-22) move into Simulation where they work alongside slope (-15% to 20%). The trainer resistance must reflect the…

REQ-0146.title: Elevation Terrain View
REQ-0146.lead: During simulation mode, the terrain view must display a cumulative elevation profile that builds in real-time, showing the mountain the rider has climbed. The area under the elevation curve must be filled with zone-colored power data, combining the "road" (slope/elevation) and "…

REQ-0147.title: Visual Interval Row Component
REQ-0147.lead: Each workout interval must be represented as a single visual row with a draggable power slider, duration stepper, and auto-derived label. Advanced fields (end power for ramps, cadence target) must be hidden by default behind an expandable toggle to reduce visual complexity.

REQ-0148.title: Live Terrain Preview
REQ-0148.lead: The workout editor must display a live terrain preview at the top that shows the workout shape and updates in real time as intervals are modified. The preview must reuse the existing WorkoutTerrainView composable and be read-only.

REQ-0149.title: Workout Preset Templates
REQ-0149.lead: The workout editor must offer preset workout templates as starting points when creating a new workout. Templates reduce the intimidation of a blank editor and provide a foundation the user can customize.

REQ-0150.title: History thread grouping — collapse repeated attempts by workoutProgramId
REQ-0150.lead: The Workout History screen shall group sessions that share a workoutProgramId into a single collapsible thread card when the group has two or more qualifying attempts for the current rider. Single-attempt workouts and free-ride sessions shall render as flat rows without a thread…

REQ-0151.title: Action-surface button layout conventions
REQ-0151.lead: Every action surface in the app that shows ≥2 buttons SHALL follow one of three layout patterns depending on the surface type, and SHALL apply a consistent ordering; destructive-styling convention within the chosen pattern. The goal is that a rider learns "where is save" once an…

REQ-0152.title: In-app language picker (Settings → Language)
REQ-0152.lead: User explicitly chooses an interface language from the Tier-1 set, independent of the device locale, with the option to follow the device locale.

REQ-0153.title: Auto-detect device locale on first launch (Tier-1 set)
REQ-0153.lead: First-launch users get their device language for free if it's in our Tier-1 set; English fallback otherwise. Explicit user choice always wins.

REQ-0154.title: All UI strings sourced from resources (no hardcoded literals)
REQ-0154.lead: Hardcoded English text is the bug; every user-visible string lives in strings.xml so the FEAT-0065 pipeline can translate it.

REQ-0155.title: Bundled workouts ship pre-translated for Tier-1 locales
REQ-0155.lead: Bundled content is build-time-translated, not runtime-translated. No-LLM users get a fully localized library out of the box.

REQ-0156.title: AI workout generator emits user-locale strings
REQ-0156.lead: The generator emits in the user's UI language. The user's prompt is naturally in their language; the model output should match.

REQ-0157.title: Imported foreign-locale workouts can be translated on demand
REQ-0157.lead: Imported workouts can be translated when the user wants — banner for the just-in-time case, toggle for power users, bulk action for locale switches.

REQ-0158.title: Runtime translation features are LLM-gated (no LLM = no surface)
REQ-0158.lead: No-LLM users see foreign-locale workouts in their original language. No nag, no broken ride, no degraded structure. The translate UI just isn't shown.

REQ-0159.title: Cached translations persist across LLM availability changes
REQ-0159.lead: Translation results are part of the workout, not a session-scoped cache. Once translated, always available — even after the user removes the LLM that produced the translation.

REQ-0160.title: Locale-aware UI rendering: plurals + max-char budgets
REQ-0160.lead: Plurals work natively; tight labels don't overflow when German / Portuguese / Italian renders 30% longer than English.

REQ-0161.title: Cycling glossary is the single source for term translations
REQ-0161.lead: One file, two consumers (build-time pipeline + runtime AI prompt), consistent terminology across bundled and generated workouts. Categorisation is research-validated against native cycling-community usage; we don't translate terms the cycling community already speaks in English,…

REQ-0162.title: Coaching cues kept minimal — only at transitions and key moments
